```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(roadmappeR)
```

## general idea

A roadmap is based on a set of milestones. Each one sits on a track of readiness levels (TRL, MRL, FRL, or anything you like), and is either on a fixed date, or
x months after one or more other milestones. 

Everything is stored in one plain csv file, see `?"milestones-format"`.

## Start from the example

```{r}
csv <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
file.copy(roadmap_example(), csv)
ms <- read_milestones(csv)
ms[, c("id", "date", "after", "status")]
```

`after` reads "after TRL 6 by 14 months and after MRL 6 by 1 month" for
`TRL6:14;MRL6:1`. Dates are computed from these rules:

```{r}
r <- resolve_milestones(ms)
r[r$id %in% c("TRL5", "TRL7", "FRL6"), c("id", "when", "driver")]
```

`driver` is the dependency that decides the date, shown as the dark arrow.

## Plot

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_roadmap(ms)
```

Hover a point to see its date, dependencies and comment (which may have several
lines).

## Move things around

In the app you drag points. In code, the same operation is
`move_milestone()`. Moving a dependent milestone rewrites the lag of its longest
dependency; everything after it follows.

```{r}
res <- move_milestone(ms, "TRL7", "2029-11-30")
res$df$after[res$df$id == "TRL7"]
```

A move that would break a dependency is refused:

```{r}
move_milestone(ms, "TRL7", "2028-09-01")$message
```

## The interactive app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_roadmap(csv)
```

- **Drag** a point sideways to move it.
- **Click** a point to edit label, status, dependencies and comment.
- **Add** milestones, or a new track by typing a new track name.

Every change is saved straight to the CSV, keeping only the latest state.

## Share the current status

```{r, eval = FALSE}
export_snapshot(csv, "roadmap_snapshot.html")
```

This writes one self-contained HTML file with hover but **no editing**.
